**KOSS CORPORATION - FOURTH AMENDMENT TO REVOLVING CREDIT AGREEMENT**

---

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**Date of Agreement:** October 30, 2024

**Borrower/Company Overview:** Koss Corporation, a Delaware corporation

**Transaction Description:** Fourth Amendment to an existing Revolving Credit Agreement originally dated May 14, 2019, between Koss Corporation (Borrower) and Town Bank, N.A. (Lender). This amendment represents the fourth modification to the original credit facility, following previous amendments in January 2021, February 2022, and October 2022.

**Purpose of Financing:** The amendment serves to extend the maturity date of the existing revolving credit note and eliminate the requirement for annual financial projections.

**Company Background and Context:** Koss Corporation is a Delaware-incorporated entity with Kim M. Schulte serving as CFO and Secretary. The company has maintained a banking relationship with Town Bank, N.A. since at least 2019 through this revolving credit facility.

---

## 2. INVESTMENT HIGHLIGHTS & RISKS

### Key Strengths / Credit Positives:
• **Established Banking Relationship** - Multi-year relationship with Town Bank dating back to 2019 demonstrates ongoing lender confidence
• **Covenant Relief** - Elimination of annual financial projection requirements suggests improved operational predictability or lender comfort with credit profile
• **Maturity Extension** - Two-year extension to October 31, 2026 provides enhanced liquidity runway and refinancing flexibility
• **Amendment History** - Regular facility amendments indicate active credit management and borrower-lender engagement

### Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:
• **Limited Financial Visibility** - Removal of annual projection requirements may reduce forward-looking financial transparency
• **Single Lender Concentration** - Reliance on Town Bank, N.A. as sole identified lender creates potential refinancing risk
• **Incomplete Documentation** - Amendment document provides limited insight into underlying facility terms, covenants, and current utilization levels

---
